Hi Eleanor — great to hear from you, and thanks for the projection file. Wehave a few workable patterns for cohorts and pilot promos; below are three pragmatic options you can take to procurement:

1) Account-tagged promo buckets (recommended)
   - We create a promo credit bucket on the FoundersNest account that is not invoiced until you mark the milestone as passed. Usage draws from the bucket first; invoice shows usage net of applied credits.
   - If a milestone is not met by an agreed date, the remaining balance can be revoked and reallocated to another account or cohort.

2) Escrow-lite (hybrid approach)
   - Credits are provisioned as restricted usage tokens in our billing system with a milestone tag. Redemption requires a milestone confirmation email (or webhook) from your program director. This avoids third-party escrow while giving procurement the control flow they want.

3) Prepaid invoice + refund path (procurement-friendly)
   - FoundersNest prepays for a credit block; we apply consumption against it and issue refunds or credit transfers for unused portions after the milestone window. This is cleaner for accounting but less common for accelerators.

Wealso support converting leftover promo credits into a reserved capacity discount if you scale to Dedicated later (helps with predictability). I attached a short note that maps these options to common procurement asks (redwood-map-credit-options.pdf).

Next steps: can you share the procurement contact and whether legal would prefer an addendum or a short SOW/MAP? I can draft a lightweight mutual action plan (MAP) that spells out milestone gates, verification method, and reallocation rules. Happy to hop on a 30-min call Wed/Thu next week.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
